symptoms: Continuous dark or bright red blood flow
first_aid_steps: Apply direct, constant pressure over the wound using a clean cloth or sterile bandage.
Elevate the injured limb above heart level if no bone fracture is suspected.
Do not remove embedded sharp objects; apply padding around them.
Call emergency services (108) if bleeding persists after 10 minutes of direct pressure.
Hold the burned area under cool running tap water for at least 15-20 minutes.
Do not apply ice, butter, toothpastes, or oil ointment on fresh burns.
Cover loosely with a clean, non-stick sterile gauze bandage.
Seek immediate emergency medical care for electrical, chemical, or face/joint burns.
Immediately wash the wound thoroughly with mild soap and running tap water for at least 15 minutes to reduce viral load.
Apply a clean antiseptic solution (like Povidone-Iodine or Dettol/Savlon) to disinfect the wound.
Press a clean cloth over the wound to stop minor bleeding.
🚨 URGENT: Visit a hospital or clinic IMMEDIATELY (within 24 hours) for Anti-Rabies Vaccine (ARV) and Tetanus Toxoid (TT) shot.
Do not stitch open animal bite wounds or apply household powders.

emergency_type: Spider & Insect Stings (Local Reaction vs Anaphylaxis)
first_aid_steps: Wash the sting area with mild soap and water.
Apply a cold compress or ice pack wrapped in a clean cloth for 10-15 minutes to reduce localized pain and swelling.
Apply Calamine lotion or hydrocortisone cream to relieve itching.
Take an OTC antihistamine (e.g., Cetirizine 10mg) for severe itching.
🚨 EMERGENCY ALERT: Seek immediate ER care (Call 108) if experiencing difficulty breathing, facial swelling, dizziness, or hives (signs of allergic Anaphylaxis).
Keep the victim calm and strictly immobile. Immobilize the bitten limb below heart level.
Remove tight rings, watches, or clothing around the bitten area before swelling starts.
DO NOT cut the wound, suck out venom, or apply tight tourniquets.
Transport the patient immediately to the nearest hospital with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV) availability.
